en.headline: HSBC launches RedCoin stablecoin for PayMe users
en.dek: The Hong Kong dollar-backed stablecoin is rolling out in stages from Friday for more than 3.3 million PayMe users, supporting peer-to-peer and merchant payments.
body: HSBC has begun introducing its Hong Kong dollar-backed stablecoin, HSBC RedCoin, to users of the PayMe app starting Friday.

The bank said the phased rollout is intended to ensure stable service for more than 3.3 million users. Once activated, the wallet supports peer-to-peer transfers and payments to participating merchants through an interface similar to the existing PayMe experience, according to PayMe head Lawrence Li.

Maggie Ng, chief executive of HSBC Hong Kong and general manager of retail banking and wealth management, described the launch as part of a broader shift of funds and assets onto digital networks. The bank plans to add the ability to subscribe to tokenised investment products, including a Hong Kong dollar money market fund, through its mobile banking app later this year.

HSBC obtained a stablecoin issuer licence from the Hong Kong Monetary Authority earlier in the year. The company has cautioned the public against any tokens claiming association with the bank that are not issued through its official channels.

zh.headline: 滙豐推出RedCoin穩定幣供PayMe用戶使用
zh.dek: 港元穩定幣由周五起分階段向逾330萬名PayMe用戶推出，支援個人對個人及商戶付款。
body: 滙豐由周五起向PayMe應用程式用戶推出其港元穩定幣滙豐RedCoin。
銀行表示，分階段推出是為確保逾330萬名用戶的服務穩定。PayMe行政總裁李冠康表示，用戶啟動錢包後，可透過與現有PayMe體驗相近的介面進行個人對個人轉賬及向參與商戶付款。
滙豐香港行政總裁兼零售銀行及財富管理總經理伍楊玉如形容，是次推出屬資金及資產轉向數碼網絡的一環。銀行計劃年內於流動理財應用程式加入以RedCoin認購代幣化投資產品的功能，包括港元貨幣市場基金。
滙豐早前已獲香港金融管理局發出穩定幣發行人牌照。銀行提醒公眾提防任何聲稱與滙豐有關但並非透過其官方渠道發行的代幣。
